c.tagline: The Biggest Little City in the World — casinos, the Truckee River, and the gateway to Lake Tahoe.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis run about $30 one-way to downtown from the airport. App-based Uber and Lyft operate citywide and are usually cheaper; there is no meaningful street-hail culture.

emergency.note: 911 is the single emergency number for police, fire, and ambulance; 311 is the non-emergency city line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: The E 4th Street corridor and blocks just east of the downtown casino core attract transients late at night; keep casino winnings discreet.

hood_desc: The neon heart of the Biggest Little City, ringed by casinos like the Eldorado, Silver Legacy, and Circus Circus and crossed by the iconic Reno Arch; the Truckee Riverwalk, restaurants, and the events center make it the classic first-timer base.

A revitalized district just south of downtown packed with murals, vintage shops, craft-cocktail bars, breweries, and buzzy independent restaurants; the city's trendiest, most walkable stretch for a young creative crowd.

The hilly area around the University of Nevada, Reno campus and Rancho San Rafael Park, home to students and families and the launch site of the Great Reno Balloon Race; residential with easy freeway access.

A newer, spread-out area of shopping centers like The Summit and Meadowood Mall, chain hotels, and gateway roads toward Mount Rose and Lake Tahoe; suits travelers with a car who want modern amenities.
lodging: Aiden by Best Western South Reno

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, sourced from Sierra Nevada snowmelt.

transit.hours: Most RTC RIDE routes run roughly 5:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with the RAPID and a few key routes running later; evening and weekend service is limited, so most visitors rely on Uber, Lyft, or a rental car after dark.
transit.note: Reno is a car-oriented city; downtown and Midtown are walkable, but reaching Lake Tahoe, the airport suburbs, or outlying attractions realistically requires a rental car or ride-hail.
transit.pay: Pay the driver in cash (exact fare) or use the RTC Washoe / Token Transit app or a reloadable RTC card; a single RIDE fare is about $2 and a 24-hour pass around $5. Buses converge on the downtown RTC 4TH STREET STATION and RTC CENTENNIAL PLAZA.

bus: RTC RIDE / RTC RAPID city buses

car.idp: Not required (US and most foreign licenses accepted)

train: Amtrak California Zephyr (downtown Reno station, daily service toward Sacramento and Chicago)

tip.r: ~18-20% at restaurants; $1-2 per drink at bars and ~15% for taxi rides.

landmarks: Reno Arch
The neon-lit gateway proclaiming 'The Biggest Little City in the World', Reno's most photographed icon glowing over Virginia Street since 1926.
National Automobile Museum
More than 200 gleaming vehicles from Bill Harrah's legendary collection, including celebrity cars and one-of-a-kind prototypes staged along nostalgic period street scenes.
Truckee Riverwalk District
A leafy downtown promenade of cafes, galleries and kayak-friendly rapids where the Truckee River threads photogenically through the heart of the city.
Nevada Museum of Art
A striking black steel building inspired by the Black Rock Desert, housing the state's premier art collection and a panoramic rooftop sculpture terrace.
Midtown District Murals
Reno's hippest quarter, where dozens of vivid street-art murals splash across vintage motels, boutiques and craft-beer bars along South Virginia Street.
Wingfield Park
An island park in the middle of the Truckee River hosting summer concerts, festivals and the churning whitewater park beloved by kayakers.
Fleischmann Planetarium and Science Center
A retro-futuristic 1963 hyperbolic-paraboloid landmark at the University of Nevada, screening star shows beneath one of America's earliest planetarium domes.
Rancho San Rafael Regional Park
Sprawling parkland beneath Peavine Mountain with the Wilbur D. May Arboretum and the launch field of September's Great Reno Balloon Race.
National Bowling Stadium
A 78-lane downtown stadium nicknamed the Taj Mahal of Tenpins, with a giant video screen, a bowling hall of fame exhibit, and a full theater.
Terry Lee Wells Nevada Discovery Museum
A hands-on downtown science center with climbing structures, a giant walk-through guitar, and exhibits on the Truckee River watershed and Nevada's mining history.

train.note: No international trains. Amtrak's California Zephyr calls once daily in each direction at the sunken downtown Reno depot on Commercial Row, running west via Truckee to Sacramento and Emeryville for the San Francisco Bay Area, and east over the Rockies to Salt Lake City, Denver and Chicago. The westbound train is scheduled in the afternoon and the eastbound in the morning, but the Zephyr frequently reaches Nevada hours late, so leave slack for onward connections. Amtrak Thruway buses fill the gaps to Sacramento and southern California.

bus.note: No international bus service. Greyhound (https://www.greyhound.com/) and FlixBus (https://www.flixbus.com/) run daily coaches from the Reno terminal on Stevenson Street to Sacramento in about 4 hours, San Francisco in 5-6, Salt Lake City and Las Vegas. RTC's INTERCITY route (https://www.rtcwashoe.com/) links Reno with Carson City for a couple of dollars, and seasonal shuttles serve the Lake Tahoe ski resorts in winter. Book online for the cheapest fares; the terminal is a short walk from the casinos downtown.

ferry.note: Reno is high desert with no navigable water and no ferry services of any kind. The nearest passenger boats are the sightseeing cruises on Lake Tahoe, about 45 minutes south by road.

full.blurb: The stunning alpine lake straddling the Nevada-California line, ~45 min southwest, for beaches, hiking, skiing, and lakeside casinos at Stateline.
full.name: Lake Tahoe

full.blurb: A striking desert lake on the Paiute reservation ~40 min north, known for its otherworldly tufa formations and cutthroat-trout fishing.
full.name: Pyramid Lake

full.blurb: Nevada's oldest settlement and the scenic Carson Valley at the foot of the Sierra, ~50 min south.
full.name: Genoa & Carson Valley

half.blurb: A preserved Comstock Lode silver-mining boomtown in the hills ~40 min south, with wooden boardwalks, saloons, and a historic railroad.
half.name: Virginia City

half.blurb: Nevada's small state capital 30 min south, with the Capitol, the Nevada State Museum, and the historic Kit Carson Trail.
